subject: CipherBank: support & security follow-up — RBAC, retention, emergency access
messages:
From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@cipherbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: CipherBank SecOps <secops@cipherbank.com>
Date: 2027-09-12 15:02 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo — logging/retention & emergency access

Jonas, thanks again for the demo today — that was helpful. Two quick areas my SecOps and Compliance leads want clarified before we move to a technical POC:

1) Data retention and logs: what logs do you retain for API calls (request metadata, full prompt, response, token-level logs)? What is the default retention window and how do we request deletion or shorter retention?

2) Support access model: we need a written summary of support access patterns (RBAC roles, just-in-time elevation, break-glass approvals). Specifically: who on Redwood can access customer data; do you have a documented approval workflow for emergency access; and are those access events audited (WORM log or SIEM integration)?

Also, CipherBank stores high-sensitivity PII in some workflows. We need to confirm whether we can pin inference to a private or dedicated deployment and have assurance about data residency (US-only).

Attaching our internal checklist — would appreciate a short reply with links to the relevant docs or a one-page summary. If helpful, we can jump on a 30-minute call with your security SME next week.

Best,
Emma
Emma Clarke
VP, Product Operations
CipherBank Ltd

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12 17:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — logging/retention & emergency access

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping Marissa (AE) and Neha (Security) so we can get concrete docs and timelines. Short answers below; I'll attach a one-page summary and our SOC2 excerpt in a follow-up.

1) Logs & retention
- Default: request/response metadata + token counts are retained for 30 days. Full prompts and response content are retained for 7 days by default on the hosted plan.
- Dedicated/Private: for Dedicated or Private deployments, retention windows are configurable by the customer (we can set 0/7/30/90/365 days) and are enforced at the control plane — we can provide a configuration rubric.
- Deletion/erasures: we support on-demand deletion requests via a ticket that triggers a verified purge; for regulated customers we support documented data retention policies tied to the deployment contract.

2) Support access & break-glass
- Roles: Engineers (SRE), Support (Tier 2), Security (Auditors) — all access requires RBAC roles mapped to Okta groups.
- Emergency Elevation: We offer a JIT (just-in-time) elevation workflow with MFA and manager approval for elevation beyond read-only metadata. Break-glass events require a 2nd approver and are time-limited (default 4 hours).
- Auditing: All console or support-initiated sessions generate audit entries (actor, timestamp, justification, duration). We push logs to customer SIEM via S3/CloudWatch or can provide streaming syslog for Private deployments. Immutable evidence can be exported for audits.

3) Residency
- Hosted: multi-region; we can pin to us-west/us-east region on Dedicated/Private. Private on-prem gives full control.

Next steps I propose:
- Neha will share a 1-page "Support Access + Retention" summary and the relevant SOC2 clause excerpt.
- Marissa will propose a POC timeline and contract-friendly retention options.
- If CipherBank wants, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our Security PM (Neha) + Solutions Engineering next Tue/Thu.

Let me know which day/time works.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
